target.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap
target.body:
Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. The Codex review classified this as P0 / impact:security with 0.96 confidence.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MEMORY.md should not be injected as a bootstrap file in shared channel (group/channel) sessions
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/group-session-memory-privacy-108881`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace.test.ts src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts src/routing/session-key.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/routing/session-key.test.ts --run
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/routing/session-key.test.ts (118 tests) 48ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  118 passed (118)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace.test.ts --run
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/workspace.test.ts (69 tests) 2809ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  69 passed (69)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts --run
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts (44 tests) 286ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  44 passed (44)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts --run
 ✓ |hooks| src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts (3 tests) 390ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**E2E pipeline verification** — full `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` with real filesystem, covering the exact session key shapes used by Telegram groups and Discord guilds in production:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/e2e-108881-verification.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ telegram group (agent:main:telegram:group:-100123) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ discord group (agent:main:discord:group:dev) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ discord guild/channel (agent:main:discord:guild-123:channel-456) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ slack group (agent:main:slack:group:general) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ feishu group (agent:main:feishu:group:oc-group) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ main session (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ telegram dm (agent:main:telegram:dm:123456) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ discord direct (agent:main:discord:direct:user1) => MEMORY.md true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

**Live chain verification** — simulates the exact production path from Telegram/Discord channel message receipt through session key construction to bootstrap file filtering, using the real production functions (`buildTelegramGroupPeerId`, `buildAgentPeerSessionKey`, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession`, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun`):

```console
$ node --import tsx live-chain-verify.mjs

=== Live Chain Verification for #108881 ===

--- Step 1: Telegram Group Session Key Construction ---
Production path: Telegram Bot API Update → buildTelegramGroupPeerId → buildAgentPeerSessionKey

buildTelegramGroupPeerId(-1001234567890) => "-1001234567890"
buildAgentPeerSessionKey({agentId:"main", channel:"telegram", peerKind:"group"}) => "agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890"
buildTelegramGroupPeerId(-1001234567890, 42) => "-1001234567890:topic:42"
buildAgentPeerSessionKey({..., peerId:"-1001234567890:topic:42"}) => "agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890:topic:42"

--- Step 2: Discord Guild Session Key Construction ---
Production path: Discord Gateway Event → buildAgentPeerSessionKey

buildAgentPeerSessionKey({agentId:"main", channel:"discord", peerKind:"group"}) => "agent:main:discord:group:dev-channel"
buildAgentPeerSessionKey({agentId:"main", channel:"discord", peerKind:"channel"}) => "agent:main:discord:channel:general"

--- Step 3: filterBootstrapFilesForSession (session-type filter) ---
PASS: Telegram group (agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Telegram topic (agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890:topic:42) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Discord group (agent:main:discord:group:dev-channel) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Discord channel (agent:main:discord:channel:general) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Telegram DM (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md preserved
PASS: Discord DM (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md preserved
PASS: Main session (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md preserved

--- Step 4: Full Pipeline — resolveBootstrapFilesForRun ---
PASS: Telegram group (agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Discord group (agent:main:discord:group:dev-channel) => MEMORY.md excluded
PASS: Telegram DM (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md present
PASS: Main session (agent:main:main) => MEMORY.md present

Chain verification: ALL PASS

Verified production call chain:
  Telegram Bot API Update
    → buildTelegramGroupPeerId()           // extensions/telegram/src/bot/helpers.ts:492
    → buildAgentPeerSessionKey()            // src/routing/session-key.ts:192
      → "agent:main:telegram:group:-1001234567890"
    → ctxPayload.SessionKey                  // src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts:498
    → resolveBootstrapContextForRun()        // src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:356
      → resolveBootstrapFilesForRun()        // src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:303
        → filterBootstrapFilesForSession()   // src/agents/workspace.ts:1169
          → isSharedChannelSessionKey()      // src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts:479
            → MEMORY.md EXCLUDED ✓
```

**Matrix-style evidence** — `isSharedChannelSessionKey` classification:

```
Session key shape                                    => Result
agent:main:telegram:group:g1                         => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:discord:group:dev                         => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:discord:channel:c1                        => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:discord:guild-123:channel-456             => true  (legacy fallback, MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:slack:group:general                       => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:feishu:group:oc-group                     => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:matrix:channel:!Room:example.org          => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:whatsapp:123@g.us                         => true  (legacy fallback, MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:signal:group:AbC123                       => true  (MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:telegram:group:-100123:thread:456         => true  (thread suffix stripped, MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:feishu:group:oc:topic:om:sender:ou        => true  (nested topic/sender, MEMORY.md excluded)
agent:main:main                                      => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
agent:main:chat:main                                 => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
agent:main:direct:user1                              => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
agent:main:telegram:dm:123456                        => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
agent:main:discord:direct:user1                      => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
agent:main:subagent:task-1                           => false (MEMORY.md excluded by subagent allowlist)
agent:main:cron:job-1                                => false (MEMORY.md excluded by cron allowlist)
undefined                                            => false (MEMORY.md preserved)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. All 9 shared channel session key types (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal + thread/legacy variants) exclude MEMORY.md from bootstrap
  2. All 5 private session key types (main, chat, direct, DM) retain MEMORY.md
  3. Hook-injected MEMORY.md is re-stripped by `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` for group sessions
  4. Hook-injected lowercase `memory.md` alias is also stripped for group sessions
  5. Subagent and cron allowlists unchanged
-  Sending a real message to a live Telegram group / Discord guild and observing the agent's response not contain private memory content. This requires running gateway + channel bot credentials which are not available in CI. The **live chain verification above** and the **canary integration tests below** prove the complete code path from `buildAgentPeerSessionKey` through `isSharedChannelSessionKey` through `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` through `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` — every production function in the critical path is exercised with real inputs and outputs.

**DM-vs-group canary integration tests** — 18 tests proving the full production session key chain (`buildAgentPeerSessionKey` → `isSharedChannelSessionKey` → `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` → `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`) with a canary workspace containing `MEMORY.md` with content `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram group (supergroup) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram group with topic thread => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram DM (per-channel-peer scope) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord guild channel => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord group DM => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord DM (per-channel-peer scope) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Slack channel => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > WhatsApp group (JID format) => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > WhatsApp DM => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Matrix channel => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Signal group => MEMORY.md false
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Agent main session (default DM scope) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram group: hook-injected MEMORY.md stripped
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord channel: hook-injected lowercase memory.md stripped
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram DM: MEMORY.md present, hook does not strip it
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord guild/channel legacy format: MEMORY.md excluded
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Feishu group with nested topic/sender: MEMORY.md excluded
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > DM-vs-group asymmetry: same workspace, different access
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  63 passed (63)
```

Key canary scenarios:
- **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`
- **DM non-regression**: A hook that adds `EXTRA.md` in a Telegram DM session — both `MEMORY.md` and `EXTRA.md` are preserved
- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — this restricts data access (removes MEMORY.md from shared sessions), which is the security fix

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: E2E pipeline test with real filesystem covering 38 test cases across all 7 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal); unit tests cover 21 session key shapes for `isSharedChannelSessionKey`; integration tests cover group session bootstrap file filtering and DM session preservation; hook bypass test verifies post-hook enforcement; bootstrap-extra-files hook compatibility verified for group sessions; **18 DM-vs-group canary integration tests** prove the full production session key chain with a canary `MEMORY.md` containing `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"` — confirming no group session can access the canary content while all DM sessions can
- Edge cases checked: Discord guild/channel legacy format, WhatsApp group JID, Telegram thread sub-session, Feishu nested topic/sender, undefined/null sessionKey, hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files, hook injecting lowercase `memory.md` alias, DM-vs-group asymmetry on same workspace

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — MEMORY.md was documented as private-session-only; this enforces the documented contract
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — This is the channel-agnostic, table-driven approach that the Codex review requested: "core should enforce that invariant generically across shared channel session shapes without adding configuration surface."
- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern
- **Alternative considered**: Telegram-specific predicate (rejected — would leave Discord/Slack/etc. unenforced); new config option (rejected — violates AGENTS.md "config bar is high" and Codex review "without adding configuration surface")

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis and code implementation for #108881 MEMORY.md cross-session privacy boundary

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Existing users who rely on MEMORY.md being available in group sessions (contrary to documented behavior).

**Mitigation**: The documented contract already states MEMORY.md is private-session-only. Memory remains accessible via `memory_search`/`memory_get` tools in group sessions. The `USER.md` file (stable shared instructions) is preserved in group sessions per `docs/channels/discord.md:290`.

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change — this enforces an existing documented contract that was previously unimplemented.
